html:
"Shogun Japan (Kamakura)" is the map's label for Japan from 1279 to 1400, under warrior governments called shogunates. The first was the Kamakura shogunate, 1185 to 1333; the map's 1400 snapshot is really the Ashikaga, or Muromachi, shogunate that followed. The chart's bar is Kamakura and Muromachi shogunates.

After winning the Genpei War, Minamoto no Yoritomo set up a military government at Kamakura, far from the imperial court in Kyoto, and took the title shogun in 1192. The emperor kept his court and rituals; the shogunate appointed the warriors who ran estates and kept order. After Yoritomo's line died out, the Hōjō family ruled as regents for the shoguns.

The Hōjō faced the Mongol invasions of 1274 and 1281. Both failed, and the second fleet was wrecked by a typhoon later called kamikaze, "divine wind". The wars brought no spoils to reward the warriors who fought them, and discontent grew. Zen and new Pure Land sects spread widely in these years.

In 1333 Emperor Go-Daigo overthrew the Kamakura shogunate. His rule lasted only three years before Ashikaga Takauji turned on him and founded the Muromachi shogunate.
